turns.user: my dumbbells only go up to 24kg each and bench is getting easy, should I just go to 40kg
turns.reply:
Not 40kg, Ashley — that is a massive jump, especially when you're pressing dumbbells. Going from 24kg to 40kg per hand is a 66% increase in load, which is a fast track to injuring your shoulders or getting pinned under the weight. 

Since your dumbbells max out at 24kg and 3x8 is starting to feel easy, we have a few ways to make that 24kg feel heavy again without needing heavier weights right away. We can slow down the tempo (adding a 3-second lowering phase), pause at the bottom of each rep, or increase the reps to 10 or 12. 

If you do want to keep pushing the heavy weight, we'd need to look at barbell work or a commercial gym setup. Are you looking to buy heavier kit, or do you want to make these 24s work for now?

turns.user: so what do I actually do next week
turns.reply:
To make those 24kg dumbbells feel heavy and keep your progression going next week, we'll slow down the tempo and add a pause at the bottom of each rep. 

Instead of just dropping the weight down, you'll use the same 24s but perform each rep like this:
1. Take 3 seconds to lower the dumbbells to your chest.
2. Pause for 1 full second at the bottom, right where the stretch is deepest.
3. Press up powerfully to the top.

This drastically increases your time under tension and takes away all momentum, making the 24kg feel significantly heavier. 

Do you want me to update your dumbbell bench press next week with this tempo change?
